what_this_is: The last recorded run of the fixture-dependent tests in tests/phase1/. They are skipped by default because the acceptance fixture's inputs are hundreds of megabytes on one machine and each build takes ~25s. 'They were run' is not checkable from a clone, so this file records when, on what, and with what result.

how_to_run_them_yourself.1_inputs: The fixture's producing code must be present at the path named by leakaudit.fixture_adapter.F2_DIR, and its inputs (zc snapshots, trades and MBO parquets for the month) must be readable by that code.
how_to_run_them_yourself.4_expected_cost: ~4 builds at ~25s each plus a ~29s input capture; about three minutes.

results.detail: The adapter's output compared exact against an unadapted fixture_corrected run: IDENTICAL on values, dtypes, shape and index.
Perturbing snap.bid_size_1 moved l1_imbalance, total_bid_depth, depth_imbalance, book_slope_bid and others. The equality check FIRED, so it is capable of detecting a corrupted adapter.

Perturbing trades.size moved net_delta, sell_volume, trade_volume, large_trade_count, net_delta_1s. The cross-frame ts_floor join is live under the adapter, which is why raw is a dict of frames rather than a single frame.
The builder assigns columns onto what it reads; the served frames are deep-copied, so the caller's raw is unchanged after a build.

last_run.negative_control: An unperturbed adapted build compared IDENTICAL to the reference, so the two known-positives above are detections and not a check that always fires.

why_a_record_and_not_an_assertion: A stranger cloning this repository sees '39 passed, 4 skipped' and cannot tell whether those four have ever passed or how to run them. A skip marker keeps a test runnable; it does not stand in for having run it. This file is the checkable part.
